spec.title: Windows context parity for Claude Code

tasks.title: Put .frame/bin on Windows PATH and name what lives there
tasks.whatChanged: launchEnv.prependFrameBin lost its supportsWrappers gate, so .frame/bin now leads the PATH of every PTY Frame spawns on Windows too — the ';' separator the function already carried finally gets reached. Two siblings joined it: wrapperFamily(platform) answers 'posix' or 'cmd', and wrapperFileName(toolId, { platform, canPassPaths }) returns the filename a tool's wrapper takes here, or '' when it earns none.
tasks.whyChanged: The gate was a category error: supportsWrappers asks whether this platform gets a POSIX wrapper for every tool, and PATH ordering is a different question — a .frame/bin that happens to be empty is a harmless first entry. wrapperFileName takes canPassPaths rather than a hardcoded 'claude only' list because a file-taking prompt flag is precisely what lets a batch wrapper stay plain; canPassPaths defaults to false so Windows opts a tool in explicitly and Codex/Gemini keep today's behaviour by construction. Both new functions take platform as a parameter, so Windows behaviour is asserted from a Mac.

verification.detail: 533 tests pass, 0 fail (19 in test/launchEnv.test.js, 8 of them new)

tasks.title: Teach Claude's launch to pass paths instead of prose
tasks.whatChanged: Claude's injection record gained promptFileFlag: '--append-system-prompt-file'. prepareLaunchAssets now also returns preambleRel and settingsRel — the same two files as project-relative, forward-slash paths. A new exported pure inlineInjectionFlags(tool, assets, platform) composes the wrapper-less branch and getLaunchCommand delegates to it, dropping its own flags.push pair and the now-unused `declared` local.
tasks.whyChanged: The composed line is typed into the PTY, and the preamble is 9 lines with 6 backticks: cmd.exe submits at the first newline and PowerShell reads a backtick as an escape, so --settings — and with it the spec-hint hooks — is the first thing lost. Two paths make the line single-line and quote-free. The paths are relative because the PTY's cwd is the project, which sidesteps a space in the path and the backslash a POSIX shell would eat. The file flag is chosen only where !supportsWrappers(platform): it has no --help row of its own, so an older CLI rejects it outright, and the POSIX path that works today must not acquire that version dependency (C3).

verification.detail: 545 tests pass, 0 fail (12 new in test/aiToolLaunch.test.js)

tasks.title: Write the .frame/bin/<id>.cmd wrapper template
tasks.whatChanged: Added getCmdWrapperTemplate(toolCommand, options) to src/shared/frameTemplates.js. It generates plain batch that resolves the real CLI with `for /f … in ('where <tool>')` skipping any hit whose %%~dpI is %~dp0, exits 127 with a stderr message when nothing remains, passes through under FRAME_NO_WRAP and when promptFileFlag is already on the line, walks up from %CD% to the directory holding .frame\, and routes every branch to one `call "%FRAME_REAL%" %FRAME_FLAGS% %*` followed by a bare `exit /b`. It returns '' for a tool with no promptFileFlag. 15 string assertions landed in test/frameTemplates.test.js.
tasks.whyChanged: The already-composed check scans arguments one at a time in a :frame_scan_args subroutine using %~1 rather than searching the whole of %* with substring substitution — that is a deviation from the plan's wording, taken because %* expands during parsing and a user argument carrying & or | would be re-parsed as syntax; %~1 strips cmd's quotes and compares a value. Exit-code propagation is goto-shaped rather than %ERRORLEVEL%-shaped because cmd.exe expands variables when it parses a parenthesised block, so the variable never appears in the file at all. Nothing executes in the tests: cmd.exe is not on this machine, and the real verification is T10's protocol.

verification.detail: 559 tests pass, 0 fail (14 new in test/frameTemplates.test.js)

tasks.title: Let writeWrapper choose its family and self-gate
tasks.whatChanged: writeWrapper now asks launchEnv for the filename (wrapperFileName with canPassPaths: !!injection.promptFileFlag) and the family (wrapperFamily), picks getCmdWrapperTemplate or getWrapperTemplate accordingly, skips the 0o755 chmod for the cmd family, and returns '' for a tool that earns no wrapper here. prepareLaunchAssets dropped its own supportsWrappers() call and simply calls it. wrapperLaunchCommand gained a comment recording why the .cmd is deliberately not the composed launch line.
tasks.whyChanged: Self-gating is what keeps generation on project open, write-if-changed and per tool (C6) while making Codex and Gemini a condition rather than a special case: they declare no promptFileFlag, so on Windows they get no file and behave exactly as they do today. The chmod is skipped because Windows resolves a .cmd through PATHEXT and fs.chmodSync there is a no-op at best. Verified by simulation: forcing win32 through launchEnv writes only .frame/bin/claude.cmd, and the POSIX path still writes all three wrappers at mode 755.

tasks.title: Give shellSetup a PowerShell family
tasks.whatChanged: shellSetup gained INIT_FILES.powershell = 'init.ps1', powershell/pwsh in FAMILY_BY_SHELL, a new exported initFamilies(platform), a PowerShell single-quoter that doubles ', and psMarkerEcho building Write-Output ('<prefix>' + '<token>'). deliveryFor lost its blanket win32 short-circuit and instead answers unsupported-shell for any family initFamilies does not list here, then answers PowerShell with a spawn-flag delivery: -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -NoExit -Command ". '<init.ps1>'; <marker echo>".
tasks.whyChanged: The old short-circuit conflated 'a family Frame knows' with 'a family Frame can deliver here'. Git Bash resolves to the posix family, whose init file defines functions pointing at extensionless wrappers Windows never writes — delivering it would set the lane up to fail rather than leave it alone; the reverse guard keeps init.ps1 off a Mac. -ExecutionPolicy Bypass is there because a Windows client machine defaults to Restricted, which blocks dot-sourcing an unsigned local .ps1; it lifts the policy for one process and touches nothing machine-wide. cmd, Git Bash and WSL now report unsupported-shell, which is silent on the lane card by design — the gate decision was that a permanently-present row reading the same thing trains the eye to ignore it.

verification.detail: 570 tests pass, 0 fail (11 new in test/shellSetup.test.js; the old 'win32 gets nothing sent' test is gone and the no-family test no longer claims pwsh)

tasks.title: Write init.ps1, and let initFamilies decide what gets written
tasks.whatChanged: getShellInitTemplate grew a powershell branch: $env:FRAME_BIN, PATH rebuilt with FRAME_BIN first and any later copy dropped, and one function per tool routing to "$env:FRAME_BIN\<id>.cmd" with a Get-Command -CommandType Application fallback. writeShellInit replaced its supportsWrappers() gate with shellSetup.initFamilies() and now passes only the tool ids that have a wrapper on this platform.
tasks.whyChanged: -CommandType Application excludes functions and aliases, which is what keeps a function named claude from finding itself — the PowerShell spelling of the POSIX file's `command <id>`. The tool-id filter matters on Windows specifically: Codex and Gemini get no .cmd there, so a function for them would delegate to a file that does not exist. Driving the loop from initFamilies rather than Object.keys(INIT_FILES) is what stops init.sh being written on Windows, where its functions would point at extensionless wrappers Frame never writes. Verified by simulation: a forced win32 run writes only init.ps1 and only a claude function; the POSIX run still writes init.sh and init.fish with all three.

verification.detail: 577 tests pass, 0 fail (7 new in test/frameTemplates.test.js)

tasks.title: Make a rejected flag cost the context, not the session
tasks.whatChanged: The bare relaunch in agentDispatch now fires on the composed flag set rather than the caller's own launchFlags, and its notice branches: dropped permission flags keep today's guided-mode wording, while a dispatch that came up bare with no caller flags says Frame's context could not be attached and suggests updating the CLI. flagsDropped is still set only for caller flags, so the prompt's guided-mode note and the autonomous-lane pin are unchanged.
tasks.whyChanged: The composed set is where Frame's own injection rides, and since T02 that can be --append-system-prompt-file — a flag with no --help row of its own, so an older CLI rejects it outright instead of ignoring it. With the old narrow gate a stale Windows install would have gone from losing its context to losing its session, which is strictly worse than the problem this spec set out to fix. This is the recorded answer to the spec's first open question. Untested by design: src/renderer/ has no DOM harness, which the plan records as the convention here.

verification.detail: 577 tests pass, 0 fail — this change is renderer-side and carries no test of its own
